claims.text: Standard laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys exhibits uncontrolled thermal gradients.
Standard laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys can produce porosity and other fabrication defects.
Standard laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys produces residual stresses.
Standard laser powder bed fusion of high-entropy alloys produces dimensional inaccuracies.
An in situ high-speed X-ray imaging system can continuously monitor melt-pool behavior and defect formation during laser powder bed fusion.
The proposed imaging system can provide real-time signals that dynamically control substrate temperature and cooling rate.
A substrate-preheating range of 400–600 °C is appropriate for the proposed intervention.
Laser powder bed fusion is applicable to high-entropy-alloy systems such as AlCoCrFeNi and CoCrFeMnNi.
Substrate preheating reduces the temperature differential between the melt pool and substrate.
Reducing the melt-pool-to-substrate temperature differential moderates the thermal profile and reduces thermal gradients.
Steep thermal gradients are responsible for porosity, residual-stress accumulation, and related defect formation in laser powder bed fusion.
Real-time X-ray detection of emerging defects can trigger cooling-rate adjustments that stabilize the melt pool.
Coordinated preheating and imaging-based cooling feedback minimizes rapid-solidification problems that cause porosity and residual-stress accumulation.
Porosity and residual-stress accumulation compromise dimensional accuracy and mechanical integrity.
Relative to standard laser powder bed fusion, the integrated intervention will significantly reduce defect density, porosity, and residual stress.
Relative to standard laser powder bed fusion, the integrated intervention will significantly improve dimensional precision.
Relative to standard laser powder bed fusion, the integrated intervention will improve tensile strength and ductility.
The intervention's effectiveness depends on laser-processing conditions and may vary with alloy composition.
The intervention is expected to work under moderate laser powers but may be limited under extreme processing conditions or in other additive-manufacturing methods.
